reviews_1s:
Unfortunately mine lasted a little over a year and then broke when I was trying to pull ravioli out of a pot of boiling water. I love strainers like this, but these particular pieces aren’t built tough enough for daily use.Do not buy this product. They do a lousy job soldering the handles, which detach from the sieveFell apart after one week! I bought these because I needed to strain soups after I recently had stomach surgery. Was only using for wonton soup to separate scallions, not even creamy thick soups, and the wires started separating from the unit. It was not longer safe to use, as it could have left small metal scraps in my soup.The sieves arrived and, as the set I had ordered before it from a supposedly different manufacturer, were far too shallow to meet my needs. The larger sieve should be able to accommodate at least 2 cups or more, but this one was so shallow, it looked like it could barely manage one. I didn't even bother to try. The pic shows my old sieve, and the new one to the right. It's half the depth...if that.

It doesn't make sense to manufacture sieves that serve little purpose, except perhaps to make money by skimping on materials. My advice would be to make sure you can see the depth of the sieve in the ad, otherwise give it a miss.1 of the strainers was broken on delivery. Going to ask for replacement.The handle broke off of the large one the first time I used it. Terrible product! Not even worth my time to try to get a refund.Ad says 6” height, I measure 2-3/4”Largest of three might hold 2 cups. These are more like “skimmers” than bowl shaped sieves. Mesh is fine enough for rinsing quinoa, but only about 1 cup at a time, no depth for swishing/stirring while rinsing.Their shape is not ideal. They easy slip off the rim of the bowl and into what I'm straining. They also are easily mishaped and difficult to fix without breaking the handle.Low quality, I would not recommend to get these onesIts a strainer so in that regard it works as intended.

The problem is the cheaply and poorly attached handle to the strainer itself. After just a few uses the handle snapped off of the strainer, leading all my food to drop into the sink. Mind you I wasn't overloading it with tons of food, its just very poorly connected. By itself the strainer doesn't give much holding room so its effectively useless.
